title: Soft preemptive prefetch windowing and bounded intake for continuous-batcher
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Continuous-batcher starvation and long-tail latency regressions were observed in mixed workloads where KV-pin heavy requests (large context + pin operations) could occupy inflight slots for long durations and prefetching logic amplified head-of-line blocking. This PR implements a bounded intake window with soft-preemptive timebounds and an explicit prefetch budget to reduce starvation while preserving the benefits of KV prefetching.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds a soft-preemptive intake window to the continuous batcher that limits concurrent prefetch/slot reservations, introduces a prefetch budget tracker per-scheduler, implements a soft lease for KV-pin ownership with reclaiming/requeue logic, and exposes new metrics and runtime feature gates to tune behavior per-deployment. Includes unit/integration tests, benchmark harness updates, and docs for observability and rollout.

Key design points: soft preemption (requeue after configurable soft_timeout rather than hard kill), per-scheduler bounded intake window (max_inflight_prefetch and window_expiry jittered to avoid synchronized churn), prefetch budget accounting (prevents a small subset of sessions from monopolizing prefetch slots), and non-blocking reclaim path that attempts to preserve KV cache warmness by partial state transfer where feasible. Config flags are added under runtime.config.batcher.* and default to conservative values.

Commits summary: listed below (4 logical commits).

Changed areas/files (high-level): runtime/batcher/continuous_scheduler.cpp, runtime/batcher/prefetch_budget.h, runtime/kv_cache/pin_lease_manager.cpp, runtime/kv_cache/pin_lease_manager.h, runtime/config/batcher_config.proto, tests/batcher/prefetch_budget_test.cc, tests/e2e/batcher_kv_mixed_workload.yaml, docs/observability/batcher-metrics.md, scripts/bench/continuous-batcher-prefetch.yml

Testing & perf: Unit tests cover lease reclaim, budget accounting, and jitter behavior. Integration/e2e run against a simulated KV-heavy harness and a mixed production trace snapshot. Benchmarks show P95 latency improvements for short (<=256 tokens) sequences under 30% KV-pin traffic and improved fairness across tenants. See perf_results field.

Rollout plan: Feature-gated by runtime.config.batcher.enable_soft_prefetch_window (default=false). Rollout strategy: enable in staging for low-traffic pools, run canaries on dedicated nodes for 48h with traffic shaping, then enable for hosted tier with a 5% -> 25% -> 100% ramp with automatic rollback on regression.

Backwards compatibility: All changes behind config flags; defaults keep current behavior. No API surface changes.

Related: references ENG-3274 (root cause analysis), ENG-3301 (prefetch budget design doc) and a Linear doc with simulation traces.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked; [x] unit tests added; [x] integration tests updated; [x] perf benchmark run and numbers recorded; [x] docs updated for metrics and tuning.

perf_results: Mixed KV-heavy trace (30% KV-pin requests): P95 latency for short requests (<=256 tokens) improved by 8.4% (380ms -> 348ms)
Tail (99th) latency reduced by 14.9% for mixed workload during sustained bursts
Throughput maintained (+2.8%) under steady-state; variance in tenant fairness reduced (measured by Jain's index improving from 0.62 -> 0.78)
CPU overhead: scheduler CPU increased by ~3% due to prefetch accounting; memory impact negligible
merge_outcome: merged via squash by Asha Patel on 2024-11-12 after CI and perf sign-off
release_notes: Introduce a feature-gated soft preemptive prefetch window and bounded intake for the continuous batcher to reduce KV-pin starvation and improve fairness; new tuning flags and metrics added; default behavior unchanged (feature disabled by default).
